snapshot.label: Finance, economics & quantitative analysis
snapshot.labelReason: The completed curriculum is organised around finance and economics with substantial mathematics, programming, data, econometrics and optimisation, rather than implying a specialist finance degree without a quantitative core.
snapshot.concept: A financial-economics direction combining money, banking and corporate finance with micro- and macroeconomics, public economics, econometrics, probability, calculus, programming, databases, machine learning and optimisation.
snapshot.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces experimental methods, marketing, consumer-product work, organisational psychology and market research with programming, database systems, computational decision-making, linear algebra and advanced calculus. It therefore retains the economics and business core while making quantitative financial and economic analysis the organising emphasis. It differs still more clearly from the behavioural route, which concentrates on psychology, marketing, persuasion and consumer response.
progression: Business Foundations precedes Strategy & Digital Transformation and Money, Banking & Finance. Mathematical Methods precedes Probability & Statistics, Linear Algebra and Advanced Calculus; programming precedes computational decision-making; accounting, economics, data and research foundations precede the final finance, econometrics and behavioural-economics work. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and all courses are offered in their assigned terms.

courses.name: Personal & Professional Development
courses.profile: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate student formation, namely, actively, consciously and ethically relating to oneself, others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhances critical thinking and independent learning. It also helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners. The course stimulates core academic skills, namely: Select and critically analyze academic sources Articulate research questions, thesis statements and arguments Improve communication skills through various forms of writing and speaking activities The course fosters personal, social and civic competencies, namely: Craft own academic and personal learning goals Critically reflect on own learning Develop effective collaborative learning approaches with peers, instructors and external partners Valuing community engagement, including the value of different knowledge types and perspectives
courses.legacyDescription: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.
courses.contribution: Removed with unsupported finance route or weak leadership-communication contribution; not used to pad retained programmes.

courses.name: Accounting & Corporate Finance
courses.profile: This course describes the most widely accepted accounting theory and practice with an emphasis on using and analyzing the information in financial statements. Students learn how to comprehend a typical corporate annual report and to use accounting as a tool in understanding how economic events affect business.
courses.legacyDescription: This course describes the most widely accepted accounting theory and practice with an emphasis on using and analyzing the information in financial statements. Students learn how to comprehend a typical corporate annual report and to use accounting as a tool in understanding how economic events affect business.
courses.contribution: Direct accounting and financial-statement analysis: interpret corporate annual reports and economic events. The actual outline does not establish a full corporate-finance syllabus.

courses.name: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
courses.profile: As we enter the “Age of AI,” this course explores AI’s business, managerial, economic, and societal implications. It is designed for UCR students with a strong interest in AI and requires no prior technical background. The course traces AI’s evolution from early research to generative AI, highlighting its capabilities and limits. Through real-world examples and business cases, students analyse AI’s impact on competitiveness, innovation, labour markets, economic growth, inequality, climate change and society. In this context, students critically examine AI governance and ethics, addressing issues such as bias, privacy, and fairness across business functions (e.g. Marketing, HR, Finance), while also exploring corporate governance and regulation more broadly.
courses.legacyDescription: This course examines how organizations are structured and evolve over time. It explores how organizational design relates to strategy, external environment, human behavior, culture, governance and performance. A particular emphasis is put on discussing the concept and enabling capabilities of organizational agility required to navigate a fast-paced world and tackle increased uncertainty.
courses.contribution: examines the economic and managerial consequences of AI and technological change

courses.name: Money, Banking & Finance
courses.profile: This course develops practical financial decision-making skills through case studies and real-world applications. Students learn to analyze financial data, assess risks, and make informed investment, budgeting, and business decisions that enhance value, financial security, and long-term planning.
courses.legacyDescription: This course develops practical financial decision-making skills through case studies and real-world applications. Students learn to analyze financial data, assess risks, and make informed investment, budgeting, and business decisions that enhance value, financial security, and long-term planning.
courses.contribution: Direct practical financial-data, risk, investment, budgeting and business-decision work. Do not infer a complete money/banking theory sequence from the title.

courses.name: Introduction to Economics
courses.profile: This course provides an introduction to the principles of economics. The first part of the course delves into microeconomics concepts, including supply and demand, game theory, theory of consumer behaviour, theory of the firm and market structure. The seco nd part of the course covers macroeconomics, beginning with an exploration of macroeconomics events and fundamental concepts such as aggregate output, unemployment and inflation rate. It then examines the dynamics of goods and financial markets in the short run.
courses.legacyDescription: Explore how individuals, firms, and societies make economic decisions. This course introduces key concepts from both microeconomics and macroeconomics, including markets, incentives, and the principles of supply and demand, and provides a foundation for analyzing real-world economic issues.
courses.contribution: provides foundational microeconomic and macroeconomic analysis of markets, firms, households and the wider economy

courses.name: International Macroeconomics
courses.profile: This course explores the economy as a whole by examining its dynamics over the short, medium, and long run. Key indicators such as national income, economic growth, inflation, and unemployment are studied. The course analyses how fiscal and monetary polici es affect the economy. It also covers business cycles, economic crises, and international trade, providing the tools needed to interpret economic data, evaluate policy decisions, and understand global economic trends.
courses.legacyDescription: Study the economy as a whole through topics such as national income, economic growth, inflation, and unemployment. Understand how governments and central banks use fiscal and monetary policies to influence economic performance over time. The course also explores business cycles, international trade, and economic crises, preparing students to evaluate policy debates and global economic trends.
courses.contribution: Direct macroeconomic study of output, growth, inflation, unemployment, fiscal/monetary policy, crises and international trade; specific exchange-rate models are not established by the outline.

courses.name: Microeconomics & Behavior
courses.profile: This course provides a comprehensive exploration of advanced topics in microeconomic theory. Structured in three parts, the course begins with an in-depth analysis of consumer behaviour, including decision-making under uncertainty, non -egoistic preferences, and cognitive limitations. The second part analyses market structures with an emphasis on imperfect competition, strategic behaviour, and the functioning of factor markets. The final part of the course covers general equilibrium and market efficiency, investigating externalities and the role of government in the economy. Throughout the course, students will engage with research papers through presentations and discussions, bridging theoretical concepts with empirical evidence.
courses.legacyDescription: Study how consumers and producers make decisions under scarcity. Explore key concepts such as rational choice, decision-making under uncertainty, and non-egoistic preferences. Analyze market structures, strategic interactions, and factor markets. Learn how markets function and examine the impact of regulation. Develop analytical tools to better understand behavior and engage with empirical research.
courses.contribution: develops advanced microeconomic analysis of choice under uncertainty, firms and markets

courses.name: Public Economics
courses.profile: This course examines the role of government in the economy, focusing on how public policy affects efficiency and equity. It explores the rationale for government intervention and key concepts such as market failure, public goods, externalities, taxation, p ublic spending, redistribution, and political economy. By combining theoretical models with empirical evidence, the course provides a framework for analysing the economic impact of public policies.
courses.legacyDescription: Investigate the role of government in the economy, focusing on how public policy influences efficiency and equity. The course covers taxation, public goods, externalities, and government spending. Combining theoretical models with empirical evidence, it evaluates how different policies affect societal welfare.
courses.contribution: examines market failure, public goods, externalities, taxation, redistribution and government intervention

courses.name: Econometrics
courses.profile: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.
courses.legacyDescription: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.
courses.contribution: provides econometric tools for causal and predictive analysis of economic data

courses.name: Behavioral Economics
courses.profile: This course integrates insights from psychology into economic theory to better understand how people make decisions. Learn how actual behavior deviates from the predictions of traditional economic models due to biases, heuristics, and framing. Through experiments, students will deepen their understanding of decision-making and its implications for economic theory and practice.
courses.legacyDescription: This course integrates insights from psychology into economic theory to better understand how people make decisions. Learn how actual behavior deviates from the predictions of traditional economic models due to biases, heuristics, and framing. Through experiments, students will deepen their understanding of decision-making and its implications for economic theory and practice.
courses.contribution: examines biases, heuristics and framing in economic decision-making

courses.name: Consumer Product Design
courses.profile: In this course you will learn how to function in a 'real-world' design and development environment. Hence, you will work in a group that mimics a design and development (d&d) team as e.g. in industry. The members of a team in this course fulfill roles similarly as occur in industrial d&d teams (e.g. chair person, secretary, ...). A team is responsible for much of its own planning. The functioning of a team involves e.g. preparing agendas for team meetings, taking minutes, planning practical work, maintaining a documentation system, etc. During the course, the instructor will NOT act as chairperson / team leader, but rather as an ‘external consultant'. During the course we will go through the various phases of the development of a consumer product: assessment of customer needs and translating these into a product concept, develop a method to make a product, both on laboratory- as on industrial scale, analyzing environmental impact, analyzing costs and proceeds. In a d&d project and hence in the course, activities are quite varied, and include interviewing potential customers, laboratory experiments, constructing quantitative mathematical model(s) of the working mechanism(s) of a product, constructing a prototype, work out how a product can be produced on an industrial scale, consider protection of intellectual property etc.. In this course, in addition to the more traditional aspects of the d&d process, special attention will be given to sustainability. This involves e.g. the nature of the materials used (natural, recycled, …), lifespan, repairability, 'circularity' etc.
courses.legacyDescription: You will learn how to function in a ‘real-world’ design and development team for consumer products. We go through the phases of design and development: probe customer needs, translate these into a product concept, develop a fabrication method, analyze sustainability, analyze costs and proceeds. Design and development involves interviewing customers, brainstorming, laboratory experiments, quantitative modeling, constructing a prototype, and considering protection of intellectual property.
courses.contribution: Specific complementary product-development work translates customer needs into design, production, cost/proceeds and sustainability decisions. It is not an additional economics theory course.

courses.name: Marketing & Consumer Engagement
courses.profile: Grounded in academic theory, real-world applications, and case studies, this course unpacks what drives consumers’ behaviour and engagement with brands, and how marketers can build customer trust responsibly. It introduces key concepts related to marketing strategy and consumer psychology and examines external forces influencing reinvention of the Marketing function, including digital and AI-driven marketing. Drawing on the work of Kotler, Aaker, Kapferer and other leading scholars, students will explore real-life case studies, develop marketing plans and learn how to create effective brand strategies for greater consumer engagement.
courses.legacyDescription: This course unpacks what drives consumer engagement with brands and how marketers build customer trust responsibly. It introduces key marketing concepts, consumer psychology, AI/technology-driven marketing innovation, and brand and communication strategies. Students will explore real-life case studies, develop a strategic marketing plan and learn how marketers build sustainable brand strategies.
courses.contribution: examines marketing strategy, consumer behaviour and customer engagement

courses.name: Strategy & Digital Transformation
courses.profile: The course explores how companies develop strategies and drive responsible digital transformation amid rapid technology change impacting the economy and society. Students develop a strategic plan, from vision to execution, and identify digital value opportunities. Using industry cases, they gain foresight into digital technologies and their impact on strategy, business models and social responsibilities.
courses.legacyDescription: The course explores how companies develop strategies and drive responsible digital transformation amid rapid technology change impacting the economy and society. Students develop a strategic plan, from vision to execution, and identify digital value opportunities. Using industry cases, they gain foresight into digital technologies and their impact on strategy, business models and social responsibilities.
courses.contribution: develops business strategy and responsible digital transformation from analysis to execution

courses.name: Market Research
courses.profile: See how companies figure out what customers love and what they don’t. You’ll plan and carry out real research, analyze what you find, and share your results. Our course shows you how to gather opinions and turn them into smart business ideas—perfect for future marketers, analysts, or entrepreneurs.
courses.legacyDescription: See how companies figure out what customers love and what they don’t. You’ll plan and carry out real research, analyze what you find, and share your results. Our course shows you how to gather opinions and turn them into smart business ideas—perfect for future marketers, analysts, or entrepreneurs.
courses.contribution: develops applied market research through data gathering, analysis and managerial recommendations

courses.name: International Business & Governance
courses.profile: This course examines the institutional, political and cultural forces shaping global businesses. It first explores how international companies operate, then centers on key global challenges including cross-border governance, corporate responsibility, geopolitical strategies and global trade. It provides a comprehensive understanding of today’s complex international business environment.
courses.legacyDescription: This course examines the institutional, political and cultural forces shaping global businesses. It first explores how international companies operate, then centers on key global challenges including cross-border governance, corporate responsibility, geopolitical strategies and global trade. It provides a comprehensive understanding of today’s complex international business environment.
courses.contribution: examines international business, institutions, governance and cross-border organisational decisions

courses.name: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations
courses.profile: In this course, you will develop a new venture idea from the ground up. No prior business experience is required – working in teams you will learn by doing, developing a startup concept from ideation through to the final pitch. Along the way, you will gain essential business and entrepreneurial skills, including design thinking, market validation and business planning. This course fosters creativity, business acumen and collaboration to drive business and social entrepreneurship.
courses.legacyDescription: Through experiential learning, students turn their own bold ideas into new ventures. No prior business expertise is required as teams work on a startup project from ideation to final pitch while gaining business and entrepreneurial skills in areas such as design thinking, business model and customer validation. The class fosters creativity and collaboration to drive business and social innovation.
courses.contribution: Specific complementary venture creation through design thinking, market validation and business planning. Its business-prerequisite role is not the substantive justification; those actual operating decisions contribute to the business strand.

courses.name: Research Methods & Statistics
courses.profile: Research Methods & Statistics is a general introduction in research methodology and statistics. The introduction to methodology includes the logics and design of research (e.g., operationalization, experimental design, sampling), and some specific techniques (e.g., laboratory research, surveys). The introduction to statistics includes descriptive and inferential statistics, covering measures of central tendency, spread, association, univariate and bivariate inferential statistics, and analysis of variance. This course includes an introduction to simple applications of multivariate statistics but most coverage of multivariate statistics and statistical modelling will be covered in the course HCBPSYC211 Statistics & Experimental Methods in Health & Behavioral Sciences. The first 9 course weeks (not including the semester break) of the course provide the theoretical background. This includes not only instruction and practice in basic research methodology and statistics, but also the planning stages of the group research projects that will dominate the latter portion of the semester. In this portion of the semester, students of each section attend two classes each week with their instructor. Project groups are formed, and these groups work together in applying newly learned concepts to their own research problem thru individually completed homework exercises, and through sharing and discussing their progress with the rest of the class. The final 6 course weeks are dedicated exclusively to group project work. This research project can fall within any academic discipline.
courses.legacyDescription: Research Methods & Statistics gives you a strong foundation in how business management—and social and behavioral sciences—move from mere practices to true fields of scientific study. You’ll learn how to plan research logically, from designing studies to working with real data using experimental and survey techniques. You’ll also study descriptive and inferential statistics, with a brief intro to multivariate tools.
courses.contribution: provides research design, sampling, statistics and empirical analysis for economic and business questions

courses.name: Leadership Communication
courses.profile: Communication and leadership are two sides of the same coin; Quintilian, the famous Roman Professor of Rhetoric, knew this when he famously declared that the best leader is ‘the good person speaking well’. At the start of this course, the participants will be introduced the main leadership and communication models and theories. They will also read leading articles from the Harvard Business Review on leadership communication. Theories that will be explored will include transformational, authentic and adaptive leadership approaches. We will also explore the roles of gender, ethics and culture in communicative leadership positions. The module will focus on the role of emotional intelligence in communicating leadership; touching on key matters such as empathy, ethics, self-awareness and self-regulation. The course will also have a distinctive liberal arts and sciences flavour to it, analysing the leadership qualities and deficiencies of characters in prose fiction, film and drama. It is especially in the worlds created by Shakespeare, where key lessons about how to lead, and how not to lead, can be learned by the leaders of tomorrow. The course will also bring in real leaders from outside the college, from both the business and public sectors, to interact with the students on the subject matter of their own communicative leadership experiences and goals. Such interactions with entrepreneurial and industry heads may lead to spin-off internships in the following academic year.
courses.legacyDescription: This course blends theory with practice from both fiction and the real world, helping you develop essential leadership skills. Learn how to inspire teams, sharpen your communication, take ethical decisions, and lead with confidence.
courses.contribution: Removed with unsupported finance route or weak leadership-communication contribution; not used to pad retained programmes.

courses.name: Psychology of Organizations & Leadership
courses.profile: People are the organisation. Without people, organisations cannot survive or be productive. This course, tailored for Liberal Arts and Sciences bachelor students, offers an interdisciplinary exploration of the psychological, social, and structural dynamics within organisations. It equips students with the knowledge and skills needed to navigate and influence organisational environments effectively throughout their academic and professional careers. Drawing on foundational and contemporary research in organisational behaviour, this upper- level undergraduate course incorporates a case-based approach that includes conceptual frameworks, case discussions, and skill-building activities. Students will explore topics such as motivation, leadership, group dynamics, and organizational culture using Robbins and Judge’s (2023) Organisational Behaviour as a primary resource. Additional literature and materials will supplement the course to provide a well-rounded perspective. Topics Covered => Core Concepts: Diversity in organisations, attitudes and job satisfaction, emotions and moods, personality and values, perception and decision-making, motivation, communication, leadership, power and politics, and conflict and negotiation. Structural Dynamics: The structure and culture of organisations, group behaviour, work teams, and organisational change. These topics are structured within a comprehensive model that defines the field of organisational behaviour and outlines its key concepts and relationships.
courses.legacyDescription: This course offers Liberal Arts and Sciences students a deep dive into the psychological, social, and structural dynamics that shape workplaces. Through interactive case discussions, simulations, and real-world insights, students develop critical skills in motivation, leadership, group dynamics, and culture. By synthesizing research and applying theory to practice, participants gain the tools to navigate and influence diverse organizational environments effectively.
courses.contribution: examines motivation, groups, organisational culture and structure through organisational psychology

courses.name: Negotiation & Strategic Thinking
courses.profile: How do you get to yes? In this course you will learn how to craft persuasive arguments, deploy the right language, negotiate more effectively, and influence decisions with confidence; whether in business, leadership, or life. The course offers an immersive, practice-driven exploration of negotiation as both an analytical discipline and a strategic interpersonal skill. Students will engage in frequent simulations, role-plays, and reflective exercises designed to build confidence and adaptability into the dynamics that shape successful agreements. The course introduces the foundational theories and frameworks that define modern negotiation practice, including BATNA (best alternative to a negotiated agreement), ZOPA analysis (zone of possible agreement), interest-based negotiation, and the dual-concern model. There will also be a focus on (i) avoiding bargaining over positions, (ii) separating people from the problem, (iii) focusing on interests not positions, (iv) inventing options for mutual gain, and (v) insisting on using objective criteria. Students will learn to diagnose negotiation structures, identify value-creation opportunities, and strategically manage trade-offs (e.g. logrolling). Core concepts such as anchoring, framing, concession patterns, and the psychology of influence will be woven throughout weekly activities. Because negotiation is inseparable from human behavior, the course integrates research from social psychology and language & communication studies.
courses.legacyDescription: How do you get to yes? In this course you will learn how to craft persuasive arguments, deploy the right language, negotiate more effectively, and influence decisions with confidence—whether in business, leadership, or life.
courses.contribution: develops negotiation, strategic interaction, framing and the psychology of influence

courses.name: Introduction to Data Science
courses.profile: Data science provides tools for extracting meaningful information from data. In this course, you develop foundational abilities in data visualization as well as data cleaning and manipulation. Next to traditional data coming in the form of tables, we explore non-traditional data types such as spatial data and text data. The course includes much hands -on work with example data sets coming from sciences, social sciences, and arts and humanities. At the end of the course, you carry out your own research project in which you apply your data analysis and visualization skills to answer a research question.

courses.name: Machine Learning
courses.profile: Machine learning concerns an ever -expanding set of tools for understanding data and making predictions. This course introduces the fundamentals of machine learning. It presents several of the most important modelling and prediction techniques, along with several relevant applications. Topics include linear regression, classification, resampling methods, shrinkage approaches, tree - based methods, support vector machines, clustering, and more. Real-world examples are used to illustrate the methods, their strengths, and their limitations.
courses.legacyDescription: Covers core machine learning techniques from linear regression to advanced tree‑based methods. Discusses strengths and weaknesses and applies methods to real data from fields like medicine, physics and economics.

courses.name: Introduction to Programming
courses.profile: This is the gateway course of Computer Science and AI studies; an introductory course in problem solving and computer programming in Python. The course begins by introducing traditional structured programming and data constructs (i.e. branching, loops, functions; tuples and lists). Then consideration is given to testing and debugging and finally the object- oriented programming constructs. During the entire semester, elements of discrete mathematics (e.g., logic, sets, enumeration) as well as certain computational problem solving techniques are also incorporated into the course material. There are classes twice a week. The first half of each class is a lecture where we learn new material, while the second half is devoted to laboratory work where students tackle programming exercises and demonstrate their work. Homework comprises weekly programming exercises and online quizzes. Two larger programming projects are undertaken. There is a written Midterm exam and a written Final exam. By the end of the course a student will have obtained a reasonable familiarity with the Python programming language as well as important concepts of discrete mathematics and computational problem solving techniques.
courses.legacyDescription: Introduces programming and computer science. Covers structured programming, data constructs, testing, debugging and object‑oriented programming with Python, and develops computational problem‑solving skills.

courses.name: Mathematical Methods
courses.profile: Mathematics is the language used to grasp understanding of, to explore, and to gain insight in any of the sciences: physics, chemistry, biology, as well as engineering. None of these can be well understood or appreciated without sufficient skills in mathematics. The aim of this introductory course in the mathematics track is to learn basic widely-used mathematical techniques, such as differentiation, various techniques for integration, complex numbers and differential equations. These techniques are put into context in projects related to real situations in the fields of physics, chemistry, biology, economics, sociology, etc. In this course students will continue to construct knowledge on their mathematical bases already founded. Students will solve many problems as homework assignments. Furthermore, two exams will assess the students for their level of understanding and their ability to solve relevant mathematical problems. A lot of class time will be used to solve and discuss textbook problems. 3
courses.legacyDescription: Introduces linear algebra (vectors, matrices, eigenvalues) and calculus (limits, differentiation, integration) to construct and solve equations. Provides problem‑solving skills applicable across disciplines.

courses.name: Linear Algebra
courses.profile: Linear algebra is the study of systems of linear equations and linear functions. Systematic methods exist to solve such systems of linear equations. Matrices and vectors are introduced as the equivalent of a system of linear equations. This equivalence allows for reducing problems involving linear combinations of vectors to questions about systems of linear equations. The spanning of a (sub)space, linear independence and linear transformations are fundamental concepts in linear algebra. Matrix operations and theorems involving matrices will provide the basic tools for handling many applications of linear algebra. The invertible matrix theorem is a theorem of particular importance. The determinant of a matrix is an important scalar quantity related to the invertibility criterion for square matrices. Furthermore, the determinant is a measure for the amount by which a linear transformation changes the area of a ﬁgure. In multi-variable calculus, this measure is deﬁned as the Jacobian of a transformation. Introducing the more abstract concept of vector spaces allows for further generalization of these ideas. Many vector spaces resemble the well-known vector space Rn. In this course, the theory of vector spaces will be applied to the processing of discrete signals (Fourier Series), diﬀerence equations and Markov chains. Eigenvalues and eigenvectors are used to understand the action of a linear transformation. Eigenvalues and eigenvectors arise naturally in diﬀerent areas of physics and mathematics.
courses.legacyDescription: Introduces systems of equations, vectors, matrices and linear spaces with emphasis on visual and conceptual understanding. Applies concepts across fields and includes hands‑on exercises using computer algebra software.

courses.name: Ethics
courses.profile: Our actions and decisions are structured by the ways we think about values, about what the good is. This course explores theories of moral reasoning, building upon historical and contemporary sources. In the first part of the course, we will examine the main theories in ethics – virtue ethics, deontology, utilitarianism – as well as questions pertaining to moral knowledge, motivation, responsibility, feminist contributions to ethical theory, the challenge of nihilism, and the relation of happiness and pleasure to ethics. The second part of the course largely focuses on practical ethics, touching upon topics such as equality, animal rights, poverty and wealth, future generations, climate change, historical injustice. We will examine our attitudes to these contentious and challenging issues, the way the topics relate to each other, and the manner in which questions in practical ethics highlight and bring into focus broader concerns pertaining to moral, political, and legal theory. Students taking the course will acquire in-depth knowledge of ethical theories, to be assessed through a mid-term exam. They will also work on developing research skills in papers and presentations, analyzing and assessing arguments from ethical theory and practical ethics while articulating an independent, informed perspective. Towards that end, throughout the term students will compose two reflection papers concerning topics in ethics, and in the second part of the term students will develop a research project comprising a final argumentative essay and a presentation.
courses.legacyDescription: Explores theories of moral reasoning—virtue ethics, deontology, utilitarianism—and discusses moral knowledge, motivation, responsibility and the relation between happiness and pleasure. Applies theories to practical issues such as animal rights, privacy, future generations, war, punishment, disability and equality.
courses.contribution: Specific complementary moral theories and argumentation concerning equality, poverty, wealth and responsibility support evaluation of economic and policy choices. This is not history or philosophy of economics in full.

courses.name: Epidemiology & Public Health
courses.profile: Public health is about changing the world. From pandemics to lifestyle-related diseases, from screening for disease to improving water and air quality, it asks: how can we improve to keep the population healthy?_x000D_ But how do we know what actually works? In this course you will dive into epidemiology: the science behind public health. You will learn how to study disease, risks, and changes over time, and how to critically evaluate evidence. Because behind every public health decision lies a question of evidence, and by the end of this course, you will be equipped to engage with it. This course invites you to look beyond the lab, the hospital, and the library, into the wider world where health is shaped. What matters most if we truly care about health, and how can we influence that?

courses.name: Introduction to Brain & Behavior
courses.profile: This 100-level course ‘Introduction to Brain & Behavior’ constitutes the Gateway Course for the Cluster Health, Cognition and Behavior: Units ‘Cognitive Science’ and ‘Clinical Psychology’. In this course you will gain foundational knowledge and essential skills that you will need in intermediate and advanced courses of these units. We will look at the various ways in which psychologists and neuroscientists have approached questions such as: Why do people behave the way they do? Can we predict behavior and mental processes in a particular situation, for example after brain damage? Is it possible to change these behaviors and mental processes? How do nature and nurture interact in the development of how we think, feel and behave? Which areas of the brain serve which function, and how do neurons communicate with each other and with the body? We will explore these complex and fascinating topics together from a neuroscientific and psychological perspective, learning about functional brain anatomy on a micro and macro scale, research methodologies and tools in the fields of Cognitive Science and Clinical Psychology, as well as main psychological theories and the relevance of main clinical skills in Psychology. The course will be organized including a combination of different methods of teaching and learning; e.g. interactive lectures, individual and team activities with a collaborative learning methodology, guest lectures, reflective activities, among others. Course outline HCBGATE102 Introduction to Brain & Behavior Page 2 of 16
courses.legacyDescription: Explores why people behave as they do and how brain injuries affect mental processes. Discusses nature and nurture, introduces brain anatomy and psychological theories, and provides a gateway to cognitive science and clinical psychology.
courses.contribution: Direct psychological and neuroscientific foundations of behaviour and mental processes, plus methods and brain-function knowledge needed for health psychology. Neural content is complementary to economic decision inquiry, not economic theory.

courses.name: Statistics & Experimental Methods
courses.profile: The course is necessary for students who want to pursue master programs in psychology and adjacent disciplines, as well as research masters in in medical domain. It is highly recommended also for all those who want to be researchers whether in data science, business analytics, market research, political science or sociology. The phenomena investigated by scientists studying humans are usually complex, thus multiple variables must be used to explain them. The theory and application of multivariate statistical models will be discussed. These models can be used to investigate the relations among many variables simultaneously, thus providing an accurate explanation of the subject of interest. The course introduces most used multivariate statistical models such as linear regression, factor analysis, analysis of (co)variance, and logistic regression. Furthermore, attention is paid to non-parametric tests. Practical application: you will learn to apply these models to data. In addition, learn how to deal with problems that occur when statistical models are used. At the end of the course, you will be able to determine which statistical model should be used to investigate different types of research questions. Furthermore, you will be able to execute the corresponding analyses and report results, conforming to APA guidelines.
courses.legacyDescription: The course is necessary for students who want to pursue master programs in psychology and adjacent disciplines, as well as research masters in the medical domain. It is highly recommended also for all those who want to be researchers in other domains. In addition to technical training, the course emphasizes clear academic communication. It will equip you with the skills necessary to apply advanced statistical techniques to real-world research problems. With a focus on practical application through case studies and data analysis projects, You will be able to choose the appropriate statistical model for various research scenarios and address common challenges in data interpretation.
courses.contribution: Direct multivariate statistics, regression, factor analysis, covariance and logistic models, non-parametric testing and reporting support empirical economics and behavioural research. The outline does not establish a separate experimental-design syllabus.

courses.name: Medical & Health Psychology
courses.profile: In th is course, Medical and Health Psychology , we will examine the complex interplay between biological, psychological, and socio-cultural factors that influence health and illness. Guided by the core principle of the field, the bio-psycho-social approach of the human being, we will explore key theories, research findings, and specific interventions within clinical health psychology, with a particular focus on the role of psychological expertise and mental health professionals in medical settings. Based on the World Health Organization’s (1948) definition of Health as a state of physical, mental and social well-being with a special emphasis in the balance between these aspects , Health Psychology is concerned with the elements that influence health and illness across the individual lifespan. It considers the implication of multiple aspects that can be combined in a complex way to promote and maintain health or to contribute for the settlement of dysfunction or illness. Therefore, This course will provide stude nts with a comprehensive understanding of these determinants and factors by addressing the following core areas: 1) Attitudes, behavior and lifestyle factors affecting health and disease; 2) Stress and the related psychosocial factors and processes associated with disease development and progression; Course outline HCBPSYC311 Medical & Health Psychology Page 2 of 11 3) Biopsychosocial factors involved in the illness experience; as well as, the long -term social and psychological implications of chronic illness; 4) Relevance of psychological interventions in medical…
courses.legacyDescription: Uses a biopsychosocial approach to explore how biological, psychological and socio‑cultural factors influence health and illness. Covers theories, research and interventions and focuses on the role of psychological expertise in medical settings.
courses.contribution: Direct study of biopsychosocial determinants of health, stress, illness and health behaviour; a specific complementary health-domain contribution, not economic evaluation of healthcare.

courses.name: Advanced Research Seminar
courses.profile: This course will introduce you to methods to perform systematic reviews and meta-analysis: the statistical analyses that are used to synthesize summary data from multiple of studies. Meta-analysis and systematic reviews are being used in many disciplines, including psychology, medicine, education, and others. Meta-Analysis and systematic reviews are very important tools in evidence based policy making as they allow to combine results of existing studies fairly objectively, to establish general treatment effect (effect size) and degree to which effect size is robust and consistent across the kinds of studies sampled. Participants will get hands-on experience in performing analyses using R. R is leading language in statistical computing. R is an open source language with huge number of individual and institutional users. The introduction to will help you the understand basics of R: program interface, syntax, variables and operations, reading data into R, accessing R packages, how to handle data structures, and create own functions. You will get acquainted with community developed packages providing common statistical analyses and practice conducting meta-analysis using R. The course is active learning oriented, with you presenting and performing preforming tasks in the class. As it is a 300 level course you are expected to take the responsibility for your learning and proactive attitude: come prepared to the class, complete homework/practice exercise and actively search answers to your questions and unclarified issues.
courses.legacyDescription: This course guides you through combining results from multiple studies using systematic reviews and meta-analysis a method now essential in psychology, medicine, social science and other disciplines. Want to know what really works? Gain hands-on skills in research synthesis that inform evidence-based policy and practice. You’ll search literature, manage data, and present findings that matter. Learn to calculate effect sizes, synthesize results and assess bias using R.
courses.contribution: Direct systematic review and meta-analysis with effect sizes and hands-on R supports evidence synthesis about behaviour and health and evidence-based policy. It is not a substitute for econometric impact evaluation.
